note: What every public create_* accepts and refuses TODAY, with the exception type it raises. `identity_over_long` and `group_over_long` are 300 characters, past the filesystem's own component limit, which is why some of them are an OSError rather than a refusal. A function whose guards refuse the bare dot, the control character and the over-long name before they reach the filesystem (`create_composition`, `create_mapping_set`) carries no `filesystem_dependent` declaration. `collisions` records that the store keeps every name: a `create_*` whose composed file name is held by a file declaring ANOTHER identity takes the nearest free `~N` collision suffix and succeeds, and only an identity already declared by content is refused. Each case's seed is exactly what the function's own `accepted_baseline` call writes (the identity renamed for the first case, under another file name for the second), and each case carries a `reason`. A `message` is a prefix: the refusal ends with the absolute path of the file that declares the identity. An unrelated file of the layer that does not parse is refused as a `ValueError` naming the layer and the file; a test over every function pins that rather than a case here, since no row seeds an unparseable file.
filesystem_dependent_note: `filesystem_dependent` names the property of the recording host's filesystem a row records, for the rows that record one; it is a DECLARATION beside the verdicts, which it does not change. The two values are described in `filesystem_dependent_properties` and `test_writer_mutations_storage.py` branches on both. What it does not reach: the six `identity_bare_dot` rows write `..yaml`, which is also a filesystem question and is left undeclared because no host has been observed refusing it - if one is, it is a row to declare, not a verdict to edit.

filesystem_dependent_properties.control-character-in-a-component: This row records that the RECORDING HOST's filesystem accepted a path component carrying U+0001 and made a real directory or file of it. It is not a property of SWCraft and not true everywhere: measured 2026-08-27 on Windows 10.0.26200, the same segment is `OSError: [WinError 123] The filename, directory name, or volume label syntax is incorrect`. The verdict below is NOT rewritten - it is what was measured where it was measured. `test_every_frozen_verdict_is_unchanged` asks the live filesystem (tools/tests/filesystem_support.accepts_path_segment) which of the two outcomes to expect; what it asserts either way is that the refusal, when there is one, comes from the filesystem and never as a ValueError out of SWCraft's composer.
filesystem_dependent_properties.over-long-component: This row records the errno the RECORDING HOST's filesystem raised for a 300-character component: ENAMETOOLONG (63 on the macOS recorder, 36 on Linux). The Windows errno for a path past MAX_PATH is UNMEASURED as of 2026-08-27 - the control-character case above aborts the replay first, so nobody has ever seen it - and none is invented here. The replay asks this filesystem for its own answer on the same segment and, where that answer is not ENAMETOOLONG, requires create_* to have failed the same way rather than asserting a literal nobody measured.
